{{Short description|none}}
This is a list of [[Argentine Primera División]] top scorers, that enumerates all players that have finished a season as top goalscorers in the top level of the [[Argentine football league system]] from 1891 (the year that the first championship was held) to date.<ref name=inleague/><ref name=yearbyyear/>

== All-time top scorers ==
The ranking includes Primera División tournaments from [[1891 Argentine Primera División|1891]] to date:<ref name=inleague>[https://www.rsssf.org/tablesa/argtops-allt.html Argentina - All-Time Topscorers in League] by Pablo Ciullini and Tomás Rodríguez on the RSSSF</ref>

== Records and statistics ==
* The youngest player ever to become top scorer in the Argentine Primera was [[Diego Maradona]] in the 1978 Metropolitano tournament at the age of 17.<ref>[https://www.clarin.com/deportes/futbol/records-imbatibles-futbol-argentino_0_H19OP1ICW.html Trece décadas (1891–2017) Los cinco récords imbatibles del fútbol argentino], ''Clarín'', by Oscar Barnade. 31 Oct 2017</ref>
* [[Héctor Scotta]] scored the most goals in a single calendar year, with 60 in [[1975 Argentine Primera División|1975]].<ref>[https://www.telam.com.ar/notas/202009/518640-scotta-el-hombre-de-los-60-goles-en-un-ano-cumple-70.html Héctor Scotta. el hombre de los 60 goles] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220119191013/https://www.telam.com.ar/notas/202009/518640-scotta-el-hombre-de-los-60-goles-en-un-ano-cumple-70.html |date=2022-01-19 }} on Télam, by JOSÉ POMMARÉS, 27 Sep 2020</ref>
* [[Arsenio Erico]] is the only player to score more than 40 goals in a single tournament, he managed the feat twice in [[1937 Argentine Primera División|1937]], with 47 goals and in [[1938 Argentine Primera División|1938]] with 43 goals.
* [[Juan Taverna]] is the player who scored the most goals in a single match (7) when his club, [[Club Atlético Banfield|Banfield]], thrashed [[Bahía Blanca]]'s [[Club Atlético Puerto Comercial|Puerto Comercial]] 13–1 at [[Estadio Florencio Sola]] on October 6, 1974.<ref>[https://alejandrofabbri.com.ar/site/juan-taverna-y-los-7-goles/ Juan Taverna y los 7 goles] by Alejandro Fabbri</ref><ref>[https://www.elgrafico.com.ar/articulo/1088/32276/1974-banfield-13---puerto-comercial-1-el-dia-que-taverna-hizo-7-goles 1974. BANFIELD 13 - PUERTO COMERCIAL 1. EL DÍA QUE TAVERNA HIZO 7 GOLES] by Jack Barski on El Gráfico, October 1974</ref>
* [[José Luis Chilavert]] is the only goalkeeper to have scored 3 goals in a match. He set the record on November 28, 1999, when [[Club Atlético Vélez Sarsfield|Vélez Sarsfield]] beat [[Ferro Carril Oeste]] 6–1 at [[José Amalfitani Stadium]] in the [[1999–2000 Argentine Primera División|1999 Apertura]]. This was not only an Argentine but a worldwide record for a goalkeeper.<ref>[https://www.pagina12.com.ar/233473-irrepetible-el-dia-que-chilavert-marco-tres-goles-en-un-mism rrepetible: el día que Chilavert marcó tres goles en un mismo partido] on Página/12, 27 Nov 2019</ref>
* Clelio Caucia of Vélez Sarsfield became the first goalkeeper to have scored in Argentine football when he scored a [[penalty kick (association football)|penalty kick]] v [[Quilmes Atlético Club|Quilmes]] on June 24, 1924.<ref>[http://talentosports.com.ar/noticia/4831/ftbol-mira-que-jugadores-hicieron-historia-en-el-campeonato-argentino/ FÚTBOL: Mirá qué jugadores hicieron historia en el campeonato argentino] on Talento Sports</ref>
* Carlos Seppaquercia of [[Club de Gimnasia y Esgrima La Plata|Gimnasia y Esgrima LP]] set the record for the fastest goal in a match, scoring on 5 seconds v [[Club Atlético Huracán|Huracán]], on March 18, 1979, at [[Estadio Juan Carmelo Zerillo]]. The match ended 1–1.<ref>[https://www.abcsaladillo.com.ar/saladillo/deportes/carlos-seppaquercia-el-gol-mas-rapido-de-la-historia-del-futbol-argentino/ Carlos Seppaquercia, el gol más rápido de la historia del fútbol argentino] on ABC Saladillo, March 18, 2021</ref><ref>[https://www.lv12.com.ar/gol/a-42-anos-del-gol-mas-rapido-del-profesionalismo-argentino-n90284 A 42 años del gol más rápido del profesionalismo argentino] on LV12, 18 Mar 2021</ref><ref>[https://www.elpatagonico.com/se-cumplen-40-anos-del-gol-mas-rapido-del-futbol-argentino-n5021262 Se cumplen 40 años del gol más rápido del fútbol argentino] El Patagónico, 17 Mar 2019</ref>
* Eduardo Maglioni scored 3 goals within 1 minute and 51 seconds playing for [[Club Atlético Independiente|Independiente]] v Gimnasia y Esgrima LP at [[Estadio Libertadores de América|"La Doble Visera" Stadium]] in a [[1973 Argentine Primera División|1973 Metropolitano]] match on March 18, 1973.<ref>[https://soydelrojo.com/el-record-guinness-de-eduardo-maglioni/ El record Guinness de Eduardo Maglioni]</ref><ref>[https://www.ellitoral.com/index.php/id_um/288161-el-reconquistense-que-hizo-tres-goles-en-menos-de-dos-minutos-eduardo-maglioni-un-delantero-record-guinnes-deportes.html El reconquistense que hizo tres goles en menos de dos minutos] on El Litoral</ref>
* [[José Sanfilippo]] (1958–1961) and [[Diego Maradona]] (1978–1980) are the only players to have been top scorers on four consecutive seasons.<ref name=yearbyyear/>
* [[Pedro Pasculli]] ([[1984 Argentine Primera División|1984 Nacional]]), and [[Diego Latorre]] and [[Darío Scotto]] (both in [[1991–92 Argentine Primera División|1992 Clausura]]) became top scorers with the fewest goals, they only needed to score 9 times to claim their titles.
* [[Carlos Bianchi]] holds the record for the longest period in the top scorers list, his first came in the [[1971 Argentine Primera División|1971 Metro]] and his last came in [[1981 Argentine Primera División|1981 Nacional]], a gap of 11 years.
* Bianchi also holds the record for the longest gap between titles, he waited nearly ten years between his 1971 Metropolitano and his 1981 Nacional titles.
* [[Martín Palermo]] holds the record for goals in a season of 19 matches. His 20 goals in the 1998 Apertura also made him the first player to average more than 1 goal per match since Juan Gómez Voglino (who is also the all-time [[Club Atlético Atlanta|Atlanta]] top scorer)<ref>[https://www.caatlanta.com.ar/archives/gomez-voglino-deseo-ver-a-atlanta-en-primera Gómez Voglino: "Deseo ver a Atlanta en Primera"], 30 Jul 2020 - C.A. Atlanta</ref> in [[1973 Argentine Primera División|1973]].
* [[Paraguay]]an Arsenio Erico and [[Uruguay]]an [[Enzo Francescoli]] are the two foreigners to have been top scorer of Argentina on the most occasions. Erico was the top scorer three consecutive seasons (1937 to 1939), while Francescoli was the top scorer in the 1984 Metropolitano, the 1985–86 season, and in the 1994 Apertura.
* [[Rolando Zárate]] and [[Mauro Zárate]] are the only brothers to have both been top scorer in the Argentine Primera ([[2003–04 Argentine Primera División|2004 Clausura]] and [[2006–07 Argentine Primera División|2006 Apertura]] respectively).
* When [[Lisandro López (footballer, born 1983)|Lisandro López]] claimed the [[2004–05 Argentine Primera División|2004 Apertura]] title, he became the first [[Racing Club de Avellaneda|Racing Club]] player to be top scorer in 35 years.
* In 2009 [[José Sand]] became the first player to become top scorer in consecutive tournaments since [[Diego Maradona]] in 1980.
